subject: Post-demo follow-up: Brightwell Diagnostics — SDK auth, routing & fallback plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Sen <aditi.sen@brightwelldiag.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Brightwell Diagnostics integration — SDK auth & routing notes

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the Brightwell team. Quick recap and suggested follow-ups from our side so we can scope the technical deep-dive next week.

High-level summary (from our demo):
- SDK + server-side auth: lightweight SDK for client integration; server-to-server auth via mTLS or token exchange (we typically recommend token exchange + short-lived tokens for browser clients).
- Routing & policy: ability to route by latency SLO, cost band, and region. We showed an example fallback chain (low-latency model -> cost-optimized quantized model -> cached response).
- Structured output / tool-calling: Redwood supports strict JSON schema validation for tool-calling responses; we also showed a sample product lookup function integration.
- Embeddings & reranker: retrieval pipeline can use dedicated embeddings deployment + a reranker model to keep token cost low while preserving accuracy.

Questions that will help us prepare the technical deep-dive:
1) Expected steady-state and peak QPS (for sizing batching/capacity).
2) Required latency SLOs (P50/P95 targets) and any hard limits.
3) Data residency / PHI constraints — can Brightwell confirm whether processing must remain strictly within US regions?
4) Do you plan to use client-side SDKs or a server-side proxy for all inference calls?

Proposed initial routing policy (high level):
- Primary: medline-llm-v2 (FP16, low-latency instance pool) — route requests with P95 latency target <= 250ms.
- Fallback 1: medline-llm-q4 (quantized) — lower cost, slightly higher latency; used when capacity constrained or for background/batch inference.
- Fallback 2: cached-prefix response (TTL 5m) — for highly repetitive triage prompts.
- Embeddings: dedicated, pinned capacity to ensure deterministic throughput; reranker runs in a separate lightweight pool.
- Region routing: US-East primary; failover region is US-West. (We will respect any strict US-only constraints you confirm.)

Attachments included: sdk-setup-guide.pdf (integration stub).

Next steps:
- Please send QPS & SLO answers (see questions above).
- Share a network diagram and whether you need mTLS or KMS integration.
- Can we schedule a 30m technical deep-dive next Thurs/ Fri? I’m proposing Thu 10am PT.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers and follow-ups from Brightwell:

Answers to your questions:
- QPS: baseline 80 rps, expected peak 200 rps, burst to 500 rps during batch ingest windows.
- Latency SLO: P95 target 250ms end-to-end (we can tolerate slightly higher for non-critical background flows).
- Data residency: Processing must remain in US regions only (no EU). We handle PHI; SOC2 + HIPAA compliance is required.
- Integration approach: we will route through a server-side proxy (not direct client SDK) — allows us to centralize auth and auditing.

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm the recommended auth flow for a server-side proxy with private deployment? We prefer short-lived tokens and integration with our KMS for keys.
- For structured output / tool-calling: we need a strong guarantee that the model's JSON output schema is enforced (we will provide example schemas). Is Redwood able to reject or flag schema violations before returning to the caller?
- Embeddings cost: can you provide a rough per-100k-vector cost estimate for the dedicated embeddings pool vs hosted bursts?

I attached the security questionnaire you requested. Also cc'ing procurement — they’ll need an initial pricing framing for embedding + LLM usage for the first-year commit.

Best,
Aditi Sen
Director, Platform Engineering
Brightwell Diagnostics

Subject: Fwd: Brightwell answers + proposed routing config

Forwarding Aditi's replies for visibility. Based on their numbers and the US-only constraint, here’s a pragmatic config we should propose (short-run / deployable within 2 weeks):

Proposed technical configuration (items for the deep-dive):
1) Auth & networking
   - Server-side proxy with token-exchange flow. Use short-lived Redwood-issued tokens (TTL 5m) and require mTLS for inter-service calls. Support KMS/HSM for key rotation (Brightwell will plug their KMS for signing).
2) Model routing & policy
   - Policy rule 1 (latency-sensitive): route requests where request.metadata.priority == "interactive" to medline-llm-v2 running on the low-latency instance pool with smaller batch windows and dynamic batching disabled for <80 token responses.
   - Policy rule 2 (cost-fallback): when primary pool CPU/GPU queue depth exceeds 75% or P95 latency > 300ms, shift to medline-llm-q4 (quantized) for non-critical/less-sensitive prompts.
   - Policy rule 3 (cache-first): if prompt prefix matches cache keys (triage templates), return cached response — TTL 300s.
3) Embeddings & reranker
   - Dedicated embeddings cluster (pinned capacity) in US-East; ingestion pipeline to batch vectors during off-peak windows to keep costs predictable. Reranker runs as a separate pooled job (smaller model, CPU-friendly).
4) Structured output / tool-calling
   - Enable strict JSON schema validation hook (we will reject and return a standardized error object if the model output fails validation). Also provide a sandbox mode to tune the LM+schema mapping during integration.
5) SLA & monitoring
   - Recommend Redwood Dedicated reservation for embeddings and primary LLM pool to guarantee throughput. Instrument with token-level traces and per-route latency dashboards.

Action items (assignments):
- Logan: capture network diagram + procurement's initial budget constraints (Aditi).
- Monica: prepare a one-page KMS/mTLS integration checklist and a cost sketch for 200/500 rps scenarios.
- Laura: draft sample JSON schemas for the triage tool-calls and a sandbox validation plan.

I attached a draft routing-policy json that we can iterate on during the call. If everyone is ok, I’ll propose Thu 10am PT for the technical deep-dive and invite Brightwell.

Thanks —
Rishi
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
